expected_behavior: Primary B1: upload calls c.req.parseBody() before checking File.size <=100MiB; multipart materialization is not bounded by that later check, despite file.stream() used in R2 put. Explain potential Worker-memory/body-buffer risk with actual order and qualified impact, not a demonstrated OOM or exact concurrency limit. A streaming R2 sink does not undo prior buffering. Safe controls: upload and hard-delete call checkAuth, reject unset/mismatched secret; hard delete is disabled unless mode hard; AUTH_KEY?: string is a type declaration and package secret:put is a secret name, neither a leaked credential. No Agents SDK/autonomous loop. normalizeObjectKey rejects parent traversal/control/reserved segments and applies configured root; show a real bypass before claiming traversal. Browser is intentionally given an operator-entered bearer credential; no evidence of unauthenticated bucket writes. Presence of CORS is not the authentication control. Memory limits are documented, runtime failure unmeasured. MIME restrictions/global spend caps are contextual suggestions, not confirmed defects.

expected_behavior:
# Hidden author ground truth: web-tools D1 To-Do subsystem
DO NOT expose this file to audit variants. Independently selected after parent requested broader D1 coverage. No cfdoctor files or prior eval results read.
Pin: brucehart/web-tools@f1a09a2e80c9d3bc62786fe06409cad0b118a045.
Scope: src/todo.ts and shared session authentication, schema, HTTP/cookie helpers, entry routing and internal seed guard. Other tool APIs and Durable Object webhook subsystem are out of scope. Raw snapshot is deliberately not a complete runnable repo.
No target source or SQL was executed. These are source proofs, not live exploit claims.

## Significant confirmed defect
D1 (P2, primary): Expired session tokens remain valid server-side and can keep accessing the protected To-Do API.
Evidence: auth.ts:189 calculates seven-day expiresAt; :190 stores expires_at; migration 0001 defines expires_at as a plain TEXT column with no expiration trigger. getSessionUser at auth.ts:15 selects by s.token alone and never filters or reads expires_at; requireUser at :23-26 trusts any returned user; every To-Do route calls requireUser. internal-test.ts also issues a one-minute expiry without changing lookup logic.
Proof input: users contains user u; sessions contains token t for u with expiry yesterday; request supplies Cookie: wt_session=t. Token-only join still returns u. Browser Max-Age=604800 controls an honest browser's cookie retention, not validity of an explicitly replayed saved cookie. 7*24*60*60 = 604800 seconds; lifetime after that is unbounded by the shown lookup until row deletion, logout or external cleanup. Do not claim logout is broken: logout deletes its presented session token.
Remediation: enforce expiry in server lookup using one canonical comparable timestamp representation; stored value is RFC-style UTC string from toUTCString, so blindly comparing lexicographically or SQLite datetime(expires_at) without format validation is not a sound patch. Optional cleanup is not a replacement for enforcement.

## Confirmed lower-severity accepted observation
D2 (P2/P3, secondary): Concurrent toggle requests can lose one toggle.
Evidence: todo.ts:170 reads completed, :173 computes inverse locally, :174-176 writes a constant, with a separate awaited D1 call.
Interleaving: initial completed=0; A reads0, B reads0, A writes1, B writes1. Final1 after two successful toggles; serial toggles would end0. D1 single-statement atomicity does not make a multi-call JS read/modify/write atomic. It matters for simultaneous signed-in clients/retries; do not claim every toggle fails. Fix with database-side completed inversion in one UPDATE, owner-scoped WHERE, and returned updated state if supported. Replacing toggle with idempotent set-state can be a deliberate API redesign.
Do not require this lower-severity issue to count the case as detecting its primary defect.

## Safe / near-miss controls and unsupported claims
C1: Every To-Do route first calls requireUser and returns unauthorized Response. getTodo includes user_id in its bound WHERE. update/delete/toggle fetch owner and return403 for wrong user. Missing user_id in the final UPDATE/DELETE alone is not evidence of an exploitable owner bypass: IDs are immutable and no owner-transfer API is shown.
C2: Dynamic UPDATE at todo.ts:139 interpolates only hard-coded field assignments accumulated by explicit if branches; all values are supplied through .bind(...values). A malicious title remains a parameter; do not report SQL injection merely because updates.join is interpolated.
C3: env.DB is present as DB in wrangler.jsonc, and migrations define users/sessions/todos/category and owner indexes. No missing-binding or missing-category-column finding when all supplied migrations are applied.
C4: internal seed route requires POST plus a nonempty configured INTERNAL_TEST_KEY matching x-internal-key before ensureSchema or inserts. Config does not set that secret. No public unauthenticated seed/backdoor claim.
C5: cookie is HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax; OAuth state has nonempty equality validation. D1 expiry omission does not imply missing OAuth state or missing cookie flags.
C6: each queried D1 statement is actually awaited through first/all/run. Bare prepare().bind() is not mistaken for execution.
C7: listTodos intentionally uses LIMIT500. Pagination/visibility above 500 can be a qualified secondary product limitation; no evidence it causes D1 result-limit failure for all users.
C8: no live deployed service was contacted. Database UUID, OAuth client ID and callback URL are public configuration identifiers, not credentials sufficient to access a DB or Google account.
C9: separate count-before-deleteCompleted may report stale deleted count under concurrency; at most a secondary correctness observation, not cross-user deletion (both statements bind userId).
C10: no Queue/R2 background path in this scope. Imported WebhookConnection reference is outside the scoped subsystem.

## Official platform references inspected (2026-11-06)
- https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/worker-api/prepared-statements/ : bind supplies parameter values; first/all/run execute and retrieve rows. Supports SQL-injection safe control.
- https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/worker-api/d1-database/ : D1 executes prepared SQL; auto-commit and batch transaction properties do not add a TTL to arbitrary expires_at columns or turn separate requests into one operation. Supports scope of D1/D2 reasoning.
